previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and a history of vascular complications was admitted for left upper extremity pain due to a dialysis graft causing steal syndrome. She underwent successful ligation of the graft and placement of a tunneled hemodialysis catheter in the left internal jugular vein. A CTA showed severe calcification of the radial and ulnar arteries bilaterally, limiting flow assessment, but no central occlusion. Hand surgery recommended outpatient evaluation for possible revascularization. She tolerated dialysis post-procedure, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for vascular and surgical care, along with management of chronic conditions including diabetes, heart failure, and peripheral vascular disease.

This happened to her once before (identical symptoms) when she started gabapentin, which she has not been taking. The tremors self resolved without intervention. Neurology thought this was likely due to metabolic deregulation. The tremors were no longer seen during her inpatient and her laboratory studies were at her recent baseline following dialysis. # Right index finger distal necrosis: Her right index finger necrosis due to her poor extremity circulation has not resolved despite medical management since ___.
